headline: High: unstructured can read/write shared documents while marker is read-only, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection risk is low because marker has no ingestion or write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem read/write, browser, MCP, or subprocess surfaces, so it cannot ingest unstructured’s outputs except through unusual manual copy-paste. Unstructured can read and write documents, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge, so hijackability is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies unstructured output into marker as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or clipboard outside these profiles, risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting raw model output into downstream prompts.
Strip instructions from extracted text before reuse.
Use a human review step before passing outputs onward.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Unstructured reads documents and writes files by default, while marker is read-only and touches no data classes in its profile. If both share a workspace, unstructured can expose document contents into files that marker may later process, creating a default-path leakage risk even without network egress from marker.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, document contents can flow from unstructured to marker via files.
IF unstructured processes sensitive documents, those contents may be exposed in intermediate artifacts.
mitigations: Use separate input and output directories.
Delete intermediate files after parsing.
Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive samples.
Run marker only on sanitized outputs.
Add file-level access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write or modify git state, but unstructured can read/write files and spawn subprocesses. The pair therefore has asymmetric overlap on shared documents; if they are co-located in one writable directory, unstructured can overwrite artifacts marker expects, causing conflicts even though marker itself cannot write.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF a shared git checkout is introduced externally, unstructured can mutate state while marker cannot coordinate locks.
mitigations: Assign each agent its own output directory.
Disable concurrent writes to shared paths.
Use atomic rename for generated files.
Run one agent at a time on the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing tool that can consume outputs from unstructured, and unstructured can emit transformed document text. If marker treats those outputs as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into downstream documents or decisions. Marker’s lack of verification surfaces makes this plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF unstructured’s extracted text is fed directly into marker without validation, errors can propagate.
IF marker is used to generate downstream deliverables from unstructured output, a single parsing mistake can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Compare extracted text against source documents.
Flag low-confidence parses for review.
Limit downstream automation to reviewed outputs.
Use checksums or provenance tags on intermediate files.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source document processors with docs-only profiles, and neither profile shows PHI handling, residency constraints, or special certifications. The main compliance concern is operational: unstructured’s document I/O could move regulated content into files that marker later processes, but the profiles do not show a direct residency or retention mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed in a shared workspace, retention and access controls must be enforced.
IF either deployment adds external API logging or retention beyond the profiles, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Process regulated data in a segregated environment.
Review retention settings for intermediate files.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Document data flow for the workspace.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
